El último electrón que entra según el or: The last electron that enters according to the filling order. Convention: the orbitals of a subshell are filled from m<sub>l</sub> = −l to +l, first with s = +½ (Hund's rule) and then with −½. Some books use the opposite order.

Cómo se escribe la configuración electró: How to write the electron configuration
<b>Principio de mínima energía (Aufbau)<: Aufbau principle (minimum energy): electrons first occupy the lowest-energy subshells, in order of increasing n + l and, if equal, the one with lower n: 1s 2s 2p 3s 3p 4s 3d 4p 5s 4d…
<b>Principio de exclusión de Pauli</b>:: Pauli exclusion principle: an orbital holds at most two electrons, with opposite spins. That is why s holds 2, p 6, d 10 and f 14.
<b>Regla de Hund</b>: en orbitales de la: Hund's rule: in orbitals of the same energy, electrons are placed first one in each orbital, with parallel spins, and then paired.
Algunos elementos se apartan del orden d: Some elements depart from the filling order because a full or half-full d or f subshell is especially stable. The most frequently asked are chromium, [Ar] 3d⁵ 4s¹ instead of 3d⁴ 4s², and copper, [Ar] 3d¹⁰ 4s¹ instead of 3d⁹ 4s². The same happens in Mo, Ag and Au.
Electrones de valencia y carga nuclear e: Valence electrons and effective nuclear charge
Los electrones de valencia son los de lo: The valence electrons are those in the subshells that take part in bonding: ns and np in main-group elements, ns and (n − 1)d in transition elements (Fe has 4s² 3d⁶, eight) and also (n − 2)f in the lanthanides and actinides. The effective nuclear charge Z<sub>eff</sub> = Z − S is what the outermost electron feels: with Slater's rules, each electron of the same group shields 0.35 (0.30 in 1s), each one of shell n − 1, 0.85, and the innermost ones, 1. For a d or f electron, all those to its left shield 1.
Cada electrón tiene cuatro: n (la capa,: Each electron has four: n (the shell, 1, 2, 3…), l (the type of subshell, from 0 to n − 1: s, p, d, f), m<sub>l</sub> (the orbital, from −l to +l) and s (the spin, +½ or −½). By the Pauli exclusion principle no two electrons of an atom have all four equal. A configuration is excited if an electron is in a higher subshell while there are vacancies below, and impossible if a subshell does not exist (2d) or has more electrons than it can hold (2p⁷).
Un anión gana electrones en el siguiente: An anion gains electrons in the next free slot. A cation loses the outermost-shell electrons first: in transition metals the 4s leave before the 3d, so Fe<sup>2+</sup> is [Ar] 3d⁶ and not [Ar] 4s² 3d⁴.
